prism.v4.3.config.CategoryOld.description:
Denotes the type of a category.
There are three types of categories: SYSTEM, INTERNAL, and USER.
This field is immutable.

metadata.description:
Opaque metadata which can be associated to a category.
It is a list of key-value pairs.
For example, for a category 'California/SanJose' we can associate a geographical coordinate based metadata like: {'latitude': '37.3382° N', 'longitude': '121.8863° W'}. The server does not validate this value nor does it enforce the uniqueness or any other constraints. It is the responsibility of the user to ensure that any semantic or syntactic constraints are retained when mutating this field.

key.description:
The key of a category when it is represented in `key:value` format. Constraints applicable when field is given in the payload during create and update: * A string of maxlength of 64 * First character must NOT be any of: `$` `/` `,` `!` `"` `#` `%` `'` `(` `)` `*` `+` `:` `;` `=` `?` `\` `|` `[` `]` `^` `&` * Remaining characters (0–63) must NOT include: `/` `,` `!` `"` `#` `%` `'` `(` `)` `*` `+` `:` `;` `=` `?` `\` `|` `[` `]` `^` `&` * Note: `$` is allowed after the first character It is a mandatory field in the payload of `createCategory` and `updateCategoryById` APIs.
This field can't be updated through `updateCategoryById` API.

value.description:
The value of a category when it is represented in `key:value` format. Constraints applicable when the field is given in the payload during create and update: * A string of max length 64 * First character must NOT be any of: `$` `/` `,` `!` `"` `#` `%` `'` `(` `)` `*` `+` `:` `;` `=` `?` `\` `|` `[` `]` `^` `&` * Remaining characters (0–63) must NOT include: `/` `,` `!` `"` `#` `%` `'` `(` `)` `*` `+` `:` `;` `=` `?` `\` `|` `[` `]` `^` `&` * Note: `$` is allowed after the first character It is a mandatory input field in the payload of `createCategory` and `updateCategoryById` APIs.
This field can be updated through `updateCategoryById` API.
Updating the value will not change the extId of the category.

description.description:
A string consisting of the description of the category as defined by the user.
Description can be optionally provided in the payload of `createCategory` and `updateCategoryById` APIs.
Description field can be updated through `updateCategoryById` API.
The server does not validate this value nor does it enforce the uniqueness or any other constraints.
It is the responsibility of the user to ensure that any semantic or syntactic constraints are retained when mutating this field.
description.example: This category is meant to be used to enforce policies specific to availability zones.

ownerUuid.description:
This field contains the UUID of a user who owns the category.
This field will be ignored if given in the payload of `createCategory` API. Hence, when a category is created, the logged-in user automatically becomes the owner of the category.
This field can be updated through `updateCategoryById` API, in which case, should be provided, UUID of a valid user is present in the system.
Validity of the user UUID can be checked by invoking the API: authn/users/{extId} in the 'Identity and Access Management' or 'IAM' namespace.
It is used for enabling RBAC access to self-owned categories.

associations.description:
This field gives basic information about resources that are associated with the category.
The results present under this field summarize the counts of various kinds of resources associated with the category.
For more detailed information about the UUIDs of the resources, please look into the field `detailedAssociations`.
This field will be ignored, if given in the payload of `updateCategoryById` or `createCategory` APIs.
This field will not be present by default in `listCategories` API, unless the parameter $expand=associations is present in the URL.

detailedAssociations.description:
This field gives detailed information about the resources which are associated with the category.
The results present under this field contain the UUIDs of the entities and policies of various kinds associated with the category.
This field will be ignored, if given in the payload of `updateCategoryById` or `createCategory` APIs.
This field will not be present by default in `listCategories` or `getCategoryById` APIs, unless the parameter $expand=detailedAssociations is present in the URL.

prism.v4.3.config.CategoryType.description:
Denotes the type of a category.
There are three types of categories: SYSTEM, INTERNAL, and USER.
This field is immutable.

x-enumDescriptions.SYSTEM:
Predefined categories contained in the system to be used by workflows visible in the UI that involve categories.
System-defined categories can't be created through the Categories API.
They are predefined in a configuration file and are created at PC bootup time.
System-defined categories can't be updated or deleted.
x-enumDescriptions.INTERNAL:
Predefined categories contained in the system to be used by internal services, APIs and workflows that involve categories.
These categories will not be visible in the UI.
However, these categories will be returned in the response of `listCategories` and `getCategoryById` APIs, and
are available for filtering as well.
Internal categories can't be created through the Categories API.
They are predefined in a configuration file and are created at PC bootup time.
Internal categories can't be updated or deleted.
x-enumDescriptions.USER:
These categories get created by users through the invocation of `createCategory` API.
User-defined categories can be updated or deleted after creation.

These entities are grouped by entity types (like VM or HOST) or policy types (like PROTECTION_POLICY or NGT_POLICY).
Each associated object contains the total entities belonging to the given entity type, count, category extId, and references (for example, for VM it will be VM UUID).

prism.v4.3.config.ResourceGroup.description:
An enum denoting the resource group.
Resources can be organised into either an entity or a policy. Hence, it supports two possible values: * ENTITY * POLICY

x-enumDescriptions.POLICY:
A ResourceGroup denoting a nutanix policy like VM host affinity policy, image placement policy, access control policy, and so on.
A category is generally associated with many entities.
The policy which is associated with this category, is then applied to those entities which are also associated with the same category.
x-enumDescriptions.ENTITY:
A ResourceGroup denoting a nutanix entity like VM, cluster, host, image, and so on.
A category is generally associated with many entities.
A policy is then applied to these entities through the category.

fqName.description:
The fully qualified name of this category. It is unique for each category.
It is a read-only field. The service constructs it from the name-parentExtId combination. An example of a fqName would be `Location/Bangalore`, where `Location` is the parent category's name and `Bangalore` is the category name.
This field is immutable.

name.description:
The short name of this category. It may not be unique for each category.
It is a mandatory field that must be specified inside the post/put request body.
This field is immutable.

parentExtId.description:
The parent category of this category (may be null if this category is not part of a hierarchy).
Each category can have at most one parent.
A parent cannot be deleted until all the children categories are deleted first.
Must be specified inside the post/put request body for child categories (if not specified, the service assumes the category to be a parent category).
This field is immutable.

userSpecifiedName.description:
The user-specified name is a string that the user can specify; with syntax and semantics controlled by the user. The server does not validate this value nor does it enforce the uniqueness or any other constraints.
It is the responsibility of the user to ensure that any semantic or syntactic constraints are retained when mutating this field. Unlike the name of the categories, which are immutable, the user name can be changed by the user to meet their needs.

description.description:
A string consisting of the description of the category as defined by the user. The server does not validate this value nor does it enforce the uniqueness or any other constraints.
It is the responsibility of the user to ensure that any semantic or syntactic constraints are retained when mutating this field.

childCategories.description:
This attribute contains the list of all the categories for which this category is the parent.
The parentExtId attributes of each child category is set as the extId of this category.
Note that this list only contains the Summary view of each child category.

ownerUuid.description:
It is a read-only field inserted into category entity at the time of category creation, and which contains the UUID of
the user who created this category. It is used for enabling authorization of a particular kind where the user has no
access to view/create/update/delete any categories other than the category created by oneself.

categoryId.description: External identifier for the given category.

count.description:
Denotes the type of a category.
There are three types of categories: SYSTEM, INTERNAL, and USER.
This field is immutable.

isStrictMode.description: If set to false, any VM configuration in the VM recovery point that cannot be restored will be dropped or reset to system defaults. This currently applies to the following fields in the VM configuration: subnets, NIC profiles, and the project. It also handles dropping unknown features on older PEs. If set to true, the restore operation will run in normal mode, where any failures will be raised as errors, and the VM will not be restored until the issues are resolved.

name.description: Name of the VM to override with. If not specified, a name is chosen by the system and returned to the task entities when complete.

description.example: VM restored from VM Recovery Point - Y

categories.description: Categories to be associated with the VM on successful restore. If not specified, the VM is provisioned without any categories.

projectExtId.description: Project to be associated with the VM on successful restore. Only the default project or the recovery point's original project can be provided in the override restore. If no project is provided, the system retains the project from the recovery point. If that project is unavailable and strictMode is set to false, the default project is used as a fallback.

ownershipInfo.description: Ownership information to restore the VM with. If not specified, the user invoking the restore operation will be the owner.

vmm.v4.3.ahv.config.VmConfigOverrideSpec.description: To override the VM configuration captured in the snapshot (VM Recovery Point). Whatever values are specified in this object, will override the corresponding VM config entry from the snapshot. For example, if a new list of NICs are specified, the existing NIC details are replaced with the provided list. If the list of NICs is set to an empty list explicitly, the VM will be created with no NICs. For the case where the NICs are not set in the override spec at all, the NICs from the captured VM config will be attempted during restore.

tags.name: ProtectionPolicies
tags.description:
A protection policy automates the process of creating and replicating recovery points. When a protection policy is configured to create local recovery points, the request includes:
- The recovery point objective
- The retention policy
- The entities that need to be protected by specifying the categories in which they are tagged.
To automate recovery point replication, you can also specify the replication location(s). In many scenarios, capturing the state of an application requires aggregating the internal state of related entities at a specific point in time. The consistency rule ensures these entities are captured in a synchronized and coordinated manner, creating a unified snapshot of the application's state.

tags.name: RecoveryPlans
tags.description:
A recovery plan orchestrates disaster recovery from the replicated recovery points of specified entities to the secondary Nutanix clusters registered to the same or different Domain manager.
The recovery plan and its sub resources created using these APIs are not accessible using V3 endpoints and similarly Recovery plan and its sub-resources created using V3 APIs are not accessible using V4 APIs.

tags.name: StoragePolicies
tags.description: Storage Policy helps in ease of storage management at scale. It brings storage configurations such as  Encryption, Data Redundancy, Compression and IOPS Throttling to the application level.

tags.name: EntitySyncPolicies
tags.description: The entity sync policy helps automate the synchronisation of entities across domain managers to ensure consistent infrastructure configurations.

tags.name: RecoveryPoints
tags.description:
A recovery point, also known as a snapshot, is a point-in-time copy of an entity such as one or more VMs,
 volume groups or a combination of both. Recovery point APIs allow you to manage the lifecycle of recovery
 points, including creation and deletion. These APIs allow you to view recovery points using the GET API
 operation and customize responses using OData filtering. You can also replicate a specific recovery point to
 a remote cluster and restore from a recovery point to create an entity. In addition, you have the option to
 change the expiration time of a recovery point, enabling either early garbage collection or extended retention
 of recovery points.

tags.name: RecoveryPlanJobs
tags.description:
Recovery Plan Job allows you to perform a failover operation using a Recovery Plan configuration.
 Recovery Plan Job APIs allow specifying configurations of the failover type, such as unplanned failover,
 planned failover, test failover and test cleanup. You can view the failover report using the GET APIs.

tags.name: ProtectedResources
tags.description: Protected resource APIs offer a protection summary and facilitate operations on protected entities, such as virtual machines (VMs) or volume groups. These entities are safeguarded through either synchronous replication or minute recovery point objective (RPO) configurations. The APIs enable you to promote an entity on a remote cluster that is part of the synchronous replication process. Additionally, they allow for the restoration of an entity within a specified time range for minutely RPO configurations.

tags.name: RecoveryPlanActions
tags.description: Recovery Plan actions allow you to perform a failover operation using a Recovery Plan configuration. Recovery Plan actions APIs allow specifying configurations of the failover type, such as unplanned failover, planned failover, test failover and test cleanup. You can view the failover report using the GET APIs.

tags.name: DataProtectionClusterCapabilities
tags.description: Data protection related capabilities of a cluster returned as pairs of capability name and boolean value.  For example SUPPORTS_NEAR_SYNC is a capability that is returned as True or False.

tags.name: EndUserLicenseAgreement
tags.description: The End User License Agreement (EULA) APIs are used internally to retrieve  the agreement text along with a list of users who have accepted it and,  to add new users to this list of users.

tags.name: Licenses
tags.description: APIs used to manage licenses on a Prism Central and clusters registered to it. These APIs can be used to apply licenses and to list license settings, applied licenses, entitlements, allowances, violations and compliance status. Additionally, these APIs can be used to fetch a list of features available under different license types.

tags.name: LicenseKeys
tags.description: The license keys APIs are utilized to manage license keys, allowing for actions such as retrieving a list of license keys, assigning them to a cluster, deleting a key, and more.  These keys are typically used in dark sites where the customer has no connection to the outside world.

tags.name: FoundationCentralConfig
tags.description: Manage global settings and configurations for Foundation Central. Use these APIs to retrieve and update Foundation Central configuration settings such as timeout configurations that control the behavior of the Foundation Central.

tags.name: ClaimTokens
tags.description: Manage claim tokens used for secure node registration with Foundation Central. Claim tokens provide a secure mechanism for nodes to authenticate and register themselves with Foundation Central during the onboarding process. Use these APIs to create, retrieve, update, and delete claim tokens, as well as retrieve the associated secrets required for node authentication.

tags.name: Nodes
tags.description: Manage the complete lifecycle of nodes in Foundation Central. Use these APIs to onboard new nodes, retrieve node details, update node configurations, and remove nodes from management. Additionally, perform node imaging operations to deploy operating systems and hypervisors, configure hardware provider settings on nodes, and refresh node information from external sources.

tags.name: HardwareProviders
tags.description: Manage integrations with external hardware providers such as bare-metal and data center management systems. Use these APIs to list available hardware providers, retrieve provider details, and manage connections to provider endpoints. Each hardware provider connection enables node discovery capabilities, allowing Foundation Central to automatically detect and onboard nodes from the connected infrastructure.

tags.name: InstallerImages
tags.description: Manage installer images used for node imaging operations in Foundation Central. Installer images contain the AOS, hypervisor or host OS software required to provision nodes. Use these APIs to register new installer images from external URLs, list available images, retrieve image details, and remove images that are no longer needed.

tags.name: PatchedImages
tags.description: Manage patched images that combine base installer images with additional patches and updates. Patched images provide a streamlined way to deploy nodes with pre-applied software updates, security patches, and custom configurations. Use these APIs to create patched images from base images, list available patched images, retrieve image details, and delete patched images.

tags.name: Config
tags.description: Manage the LCM framework configuration for a cluster. The configuration controls settings such as the LCM repository URL, auto-inventory scheduling, HTTPS enforcement, and connectivity mode (connected-site vs. dark-site). Use GET /config to retrieve the current configuration and PUT /config to update it. Changing the configuration returns an asynchronous task reference. The X-Cluster-Id header can be used to target a specific Prism Element cluster when operating from Prism Central. See the Config model for the full list of configurable and read-only properties.

tags.name: Entities
tags.description: Query the software and firmware entities discovered by LCM on a cluster. Entities represent individual upgradable components such as AOS, AHV, NCC, BMC firmware, BIOS, and disk firmware. Each entity includes its current version, available upgrade versions, location (node or cluster scope), and dependency information. Use GET /entities to list all entities with support for pagination, filtering, sorting, and field projection. Use GET /entities/{extId} to retrieve a single entity by its identifier. Use POST /entities/$actions/export to export the full entity inventory as a downloadable file. Entities are populated by the Inventory operation (POST /$actions/inventory); if no inventory has been run, the entities list will be empty. To preload upgrade images for entities before an upgrade, use POST /$actions/preload-artifacts.

tags.name: Notifications
tags.description: Compute and retrieve upgrade notifications that describe the impact of a planned upgrade on cluster nodes and entities. Notifications inform the user about disruptive actions (such as host reboots, VM migrations, or maintenance-mode entry) that will occur during the upgrade. To generate notifications, first call POST /$actions/compute-notifications with the intended entity update specifications. This returns an asynchronous task; once the task completes, retrieve the resource identifier from the task completion_details and use GET /notifications/{extId} to fetch the computed notification results. Notifications include severity levels (INFO, WARNING, NOTICE) and are grouped by entity or location.

tags.name: Recommendations
tags.description: Compute and retrieve upgrade recommendations for a set of entities. Recommendations resolve dependencies, identify additional required updates, and produce a validated list of entity-update specifications ready for use in prechecks and upgrades. To generate recommendations, call POST /$actions/compute-recommendations with one of four input types: entity types (SOFTWARE/FIRMWARE), target entities, entity update specs, or deploy specs. This returns an asynchronous task; once the task completes, retrieve the resource identifier from the task completion_details and use GET /recommendations/{extId} to fetch the computed recommendation results. The result includes the resolved entityUpdateSpecs, any skipped, modifiable, or addable entities, and deployable versions.

tags.name: Upgrades
tags.description: Perform an upgrade operation to update one or more LCM entities to their target versions. Before invoking an upgrade, run an inventory (POST /$actions/inventory) to discover entities, compute recommendations (POST /$actions/compute-recommendations) to resolve dependencies, and optionally run prechecks (POST /$actions/prechecks) to validate readiness. The upgrade endpoint (POST /$actions/upgrade) accepts an UpgradeSpec containing entityUpdateSpecs (entity UUID and target version pairs), optional management server credentials for ESX/Hyper-V clusters, and auto-handle flags for VM management during maintenance mode. The operation returns an asynchronous task reference; monitor the task via the Prism tasks API. Use GET /status to check whether an upgrade is already in progress on the cluster.

tags.name: Prechecks
tags.description: Run pre-upgrade validation checks to verify that the cluster and its entities are ready for an upgrade. Prechecks detect conditions that would cause an upgrade to fail, such as insufficient disk space, incompatible configurations, or pinned VMs that cannot be migrated. Call POST /$actions/prechecks with a PrechecksSpec containing the same entityUpdateSpecs you intend to pass to the upgrade endpoint. The operation returns an asynchronous task reference; inspect the task result to determine whether all prechecks passed. If prechecks fail, address the reported issues before proceeding to upgrade (POST /$actions/upgrade). The skippedPrecheckFlags field can be used to bypass specific prechecks such as the pinned-VM check.

tags.name: Inventory
tags.description: Trigger an inventory operation to discover all upgradable software and firmware entities on a cluster. Inventory scans the cluster nodes, identifies installed components and their versions, and checks the configured LCM repository for available updates. Call POST /$actions/inventory to start the operation; an optional InventorySpec body allows you to specify the inventory type (FULL, SOFTWARE, NODE, or RESCAN) and provide vendor management credentials for third-party hardware. The operation returns an asynchronous task reference. Once inventory completes, the discovered entities are available via GET /entities and the cluster summary is updated in GET /lcm-summaries. Inventory must be run at least once before computing recommendations or performing upgrades.

tags.name: Images
tags.description: Query the LCM images that have been downloaded to the cluster for use in upgrades. An image represents one or more binary files (ISO, tar, firmware payload) associated with a specific entity class, model, and version. Images are downloaded automatically during an upgrade or can be pre-staged using the preload-artifacts operation (POST /$actions/preload-artifacts). Use GET /images to list all downloaded images with support for pagination, filtering, sorting, and field projection. Each image includes file metadata (size, checksum, file path) and release notes.

tags.name: Status
tags.description: Retrieve the current operational status of the LCM framework on a cluster. The status includes the installed LCM framework version, whether a framework update is available, any in-progress operation (inventory, prechecks, upgrade, or upload) with its task identifier, the cancel-intent flag, URL accessibility, connectivity type, and restricted-mode information. Use GET /status before starting a new operation to confirm no conflicting operation is already running. The X-Cluster-Id header can be used to target a specific Prism Element cluster.

tags.name: LcmSummaries
tags.description: Retrieve high-level summaries of LCM state across one or more clusters in a Prism Central environment. Each summary includes the installed LCM version, available framework version, hardware vendor, connectivity type, cluster capabilities (such as MCL inventory/upgrade support), and indicators for URL accessibility and available upgrades. Use GET /lcm-summaries to list summaries for all registered clusters with support for pagination, filtering, sorting, and field projection. Use GET /lcm-summaries/{extId} to retrieve the summary for a specific cluster. Summaries are updated after each inventory or upgrade operation.

tags.name: UpgradeSelections
tags.description: Manage saved upgrade selections for dark-site upgrade workflows. An upgrade selection captures the set of entityUpdateSpecs (entity UUID and target version pairs) that a user intends to upgrade on a specific cluster. Use POST /upgrade-selections to save a selection, GET /upgrade-selections to list saved selections, and GET /upgrade-selections/{extId} to retrieve a specific selection. Use POST /upgrade-selections/{extId}/$actions/export to generate a download_helper.zip file containing scripts and instructions for downloading the required dark-site bundles from the Nutanix Portal. Once bundles are uploaded to the cluster, the selection status transitions from PENDING_UPLOAD to UPGRADE_READY, and the user can proceed with prechecks and upgrade using the saved entityUpdateSpecs. Use DELETE /upgrade-selections/{extId} to remove a selection that is no longer needed.

tags.name: LcmHistories
tags.description: Query the history of LCM operations (inventory, upgrade, bundle upload) performed across all clusters in a Prism Central environment. Each history entry records the operation type, start and end times, overall status, the user who initiated the operation, the LCM framework version at the time of execution, and detailed component information (entities upgraded, versions, per-entity status). Use GET /lcm-histories to list history entries with support for pagination, filtering (by operation type, status, cluster, time range), sorting, and field projection. Use GET /lcm-histories/{extId} to retrieve a single history entry. Use POST /lcm-histories/$actions/export to export history data as a downloadable file.

tags.name: Bundles
tags.description: Manage LCM upgrade bundles on a cluster. A bundle is a packaged archive containing one or more upgrade images for software or firmware entities. Bundles are used primarily in dark-site environments where the cluster does not have direct internet connectivity. Use POST /bundles to upload a new bundle (specifying the vendor, type, and optional URL source or checksum). Use GET /bundles to list all bundles on the cluster with support for pagination, filtering, sorting, and field projection. Use GET /bundles/{extId} to retrieve details of a specific bundle. Use DELETE /bundles/{extId} to remove a bundle that is no longer needed. After uploading a bundle, run an inventory (POST /$actions/inventory) to discover the newly available updates.

tags.name: AddressGroups
tags.description: An Address Group is a logical group of one or more IP Addresses or ranges. An Address Group, once created, can be used while creating network security policies. You can manage the Address Groups using these APIs.

tags.name: ServiceGroups
tags.description: A Service Group is a logical group of protocol-port combinations. A custom Service Group, once created, can be used while creating network security policies. You can manage the Service Groups using these APIs.

tags.name: NetworkSecurityPolicies
tags.description: A Network Security Policy is a set of rules configured to protect entities across the network. You can use these APIs to create different types of policies such as Application, Isolation, and Quarantine with Inbound/Outbound as categories, IP Addresses or ranges, CIDR blocks, subnets and/or Address Groups/Service Groups.

tags.name: DirectoryServerConfigs
tags.description: You can use these APIs to import User Groups from Active Directory into Prism Central as Categories. VDI policies can be configured around these categories.

tags.name: EntityGroups
tags.description: An Entity Group is a logical group of entities supported by flow network security policies. Once created, an Entity Group can be referenced in the network security policies. You can manage the Entity Groups using these APIs.

tags.name: ClusterLogs
tags.description: The cluster logs APIs can collect logs and configuration files from Controller VMs and various other services.

tags.name: Alerts
tags.description: Alerts or Alert Email Configuration may be fetched, updated, or managed using these APIs.

tags.name: Audits
tags.description: Audits may be fetched using these APIs.

tags.name: Events
tags.description: Events may be fetched using these APIs.

tags.name: SystemDefinedPolicies
tags.description: The system-defined alert policies can be utilized to fetch or manage using these APIs.

tags.name: UserDefinedPolicies
tags.description: User-Defined Alert policies may be fetched or managed using these APIs.

tags.name: ExternalRepositories
tags.description: A repository of data that is external to AOS, accessible over a specified protocol (for example, NFSv3) - typically identified by the IP address at which the storage is available on the network and optionally a relative path from the root of the storage system.

tags.name: RegisteredDomains
tags.description: The registered domain APIs allow users to configure and manage registered domains. Users can create, list, fetch, update, and delete these domains.

tags.name: Locations
tags.description: The locations represent geographical position. Entities that need to be bound to geographical position can refer to this.

tags.name: LocalDomain
tags.description: The local domain APIs allow users to fetch and perform operations on the local domain. Users can execute fetch, register, and deregister operations within the local domain.

tags.name: BgpSessions
tags.description: BGP (Border Gateway Protocol) gateways automate the exchange of externally routable IP address/prefix (ERP), routes, and IP address/prefix sets of infrastructure routers.

tags.name: BgpRoutes
tags.description: In the intricate tapestry of networking protocols, the Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) stands as a beacon of intelligence and adaptability. BGP routes are managed through BGP sessions, and they can fall into one of three categories: received, received but ignored, or advertised. Each BGP route includes a destination and a nexthop IP address.

tags.name: ClusterCapabilities
tags.description: Networking-related capabilities of a cluster returned as pairs of capability name and boolean value. For example SUPPORTS_SPAN_V2 is a capability that is returned as True or False.

tags.name: FloatingIps
tags.description: Floating IP addresses are accessible from the Internet. A Floating IP address is associated with the private IP address of the virtual NIC of the VM. This association makes the VM accessible from the Internet.

tags.name: Gateways
tags.description: Network Gateway VMs are used to create VPN, VTEP, or BGP gateways to connect subnets using VPN connections, Layer2 subnet extensions over VPN or VTEP, or BGP sessions.

tags.name: IPFIXExporters
tags.description: The service that exports IPFIX messages of the operations and data associated with flows in AHV clusters.

tags.name: Layer2Stretches
tags.description: Represents the operations involved in stretching of a Layer2 (L2) network between two racks in the same datacenter.

tags.name: LoadBalancerSessions
tags.description: Load Balancer sessions belonging to a Virtual Private Cloud.

tags.name: MacAddresses
tags.description: MAC addresses and their Layer2 stretch properties include details about the remote VTEP (Virtual Tunnel Endpoint) gateway.

tags.name: NetworkControllers
tags.description: A Network Controller provides advanced networking capabilities, manages and controls configuration, monitoring and optimization of network resources for Flow Virtual Networking VPCs and VLAN subnets.

tags.name: NicProfiles
tags.description: A NIC Profile is a configuration template that defines capabilities, such as SR-IOV or DP offload, which can be applied to host NICs.

tags.name: RemoteEntities
tags.description: Represents info about remote subnets (VLAN IDs, etc), VPN connections (clusters, VPCs, etc), and VTEP gateways (VXLAN, etc).

tags.name: Routes
tags.description: Routes are associated with a route table and can be either active or inactive in the forwarding plane. Each route has a priority and must be categorized as dynamic, status, or local. Clients can only create, update, or delete static routes. Every route has a specified destination and nexthop.

tags.name: RouteTables
tags.description: Represents the routing tables used and operations on them. These tables include VPC and cluster information.

tags.name: RoutingPolicies
tags.description: The Network Controller uses policy based routing on VPC networks. A Routing Policy belongs to a VPC and is described by one or more match rules and actions.

tags.name: Subnets
tags.description: Network subnet configuration and usage status.

tags.name: SubnetMigrations
tags.description: Operations to migrate VLAN Basic subnets to VLAN Advanced subnets, or migrate vNICs from VLAN subnets to overlay subnets.

tags.name: TrafficMirrors
tags.description: Mirroring of traffic from a set of source ports to a set of destination ports.

tags.name: UplinkBonds
tags.description: Uplink Bonds group host NICs to function as a singular entity.

tags.name: VirtualSwitches
tags.description: Virtual Switches manage multiple bridges and uplinks in Prism. A Virtual Switch defines a collection of AHV nodes and the uplink ports on each node.

tags.name: Vpcs
tags.description: A Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) is an independent and isolated IP address space that functions as a logically isolated virtual network.

tags.name: VpcVirtualSwitchMappings
tags.description: Describes the VPC Virtual Switch mappings traffic configuration.

tags.name: VpnConnections
tags.description: VPN Connections are managed with create, update, delete, and get operations. The VPN Connection's received route priority is assigned to routes received on this VPN connection over eBGP. Routes with higher priority value take precedence in the VPC route table. The gateways are assigned either the acceptor or initiator role via the VPN Connection. IPSec, DPD, and QoS are also configured as part of the VPN Connection.

tags.name: Categories
tags.description:
Categories are key-value pair constructs used to tag entities and policies.
Keys are used to group functionally similar categories.
Policy engines use categories to get all entities tagged to a category and apply policies on them.
Some examples are marking VMs for restoration and backup, protecting 
volume groups based on categories, narrowing or denying authorization to a user,
to entities marked by a category, logically grouping entities in the UI for convenience, and so on.

tags.name: DomainManager
tags.description: The domain manager represents the multi-cluster manager, responsible for managing  (registering/viewing) multiple Nutanix clusters to provide a single, centralized management  interface. It has support for backup and restore of domain manager on clusters as well as  s3-compatible object stores. It also exposes the ability manage the lifecycle of multiple  opt-in products such as Intelligent Ops, Leap, and Flow networking, and so on.

tags.name: Tasks
tags.description: Tasks are primarily a way of asynchronously executing operations. Tasks persistently record the intent,  progress, and other relevant information about the long-running operations. Users can interact with  tasks in the system using these APIs.

tags.name: Batches
tags.description: Provides an ability to submit batches of operations that can be performed asynchronously.  Status of submitted batches can be checked by querying the task returned as a result of the submission. Additionally history of all submitted batches in the past 90 days can be listed through a list operation. A Limit of 500 elements is enforced during submission of the batch.

tags.name: Vm
tags.description: A virtual machine (VM) is a digital environment that operates as a virtual compute resource on a physical server. It uses software to run and deploy applications instead of a physical computer system. One server or host can support multiple VMs or guests running simultaneously. The APIs under VM are used for creating and managing virtual machines on AHV.

tags.name: EsxiVm
tags.description: The ESXi VM APIs are used to manage virtual machines on ESXi.

tags.name: Stats
tags.description: The APIs provide functionality to fetch statistics for AHV Virtual machines. Users can utilize the list/get VM stats APIs to retrieve comprehensive statistics, including specific metrics for disks and NICs attached to the VMs. The APIs support querying data within a specified time range by allowing users to specify start and end times. In addition, users can specify the sample interval, apply filters, and perform various aggregations such as AVG, SUM, COUNT, MIN, and MAX on the retrieved data.

tags.name: EsxiStats
tags.description: The APIs provide functionality to fetch statistics for ESXi Virtual machines. Users can utilize the list/get VM stats APIs to retrieve comprehensive statistics, including specific metrics for disks and NICs attached to the VMs. The APIs support querying data within a specified time range by allowing users to specify start and end times. In addition, users can specify the sample interval, apply filters, and perform various aggregations such as AVG, SUM, COUNT, MIN, and MAX on the retrieved data.

tags.name: VmAntiAffinityPolicies
tags.description: The VM-VM anti-affinity policy is used to specify anti-affinity between the AHV virtual machines. The VM-VM anti-affinity policy keeps the specified virtual machines apart in such a way that when a problem occurs with one host, you should not lose both the virtual machines. The VM-VM anti-affinity policy APIs are used to manage these policies.

tags.name: VmHostAffinityPolicies
tags.description: APIs for managing VM-Host Affinity Policies.

tags.name: VmRecoveryPoints
tags.description: APIs for managing the AHV VM Recovery Point entity. A VM recovery point is a snapshot of a VM at a specific point in time.

tags.name: VmGuestCustomizationProfiles
tags.description: APIs for managing VM Guest Customization Profiles.

tags.name: VmStartupPolicies
tags.description: The VM Startup policies can be used to configure dependencies between groups of VMs. During an HA event or Cluster restart event, these policies would be honoured to start the VMs in the order as specified by the dependencies.

tags.name: TemplatePlacementPolicies
tags.description: APIs for managing Template Placement Policies.

tags.name: VmProfile
tags.description: APIs for managing VM Profiles.

tags.name: GuestRebootPolicies
tags.description: APIs for managing Guest Reboot Policies.

tags.name: Templates
tags.description: It enables the creation and management of templates from AHV virtual machines, as well as the deployment of VMs from these templates across multiple clusters. These templates include versioned configurations and disks, which can be replicated to other clusters when necessary.

tags.name: Ovas
tags.description: Enables the creation and management of OVAs through upload or VM export and facilitates the deployment of VMs from OVAs across clusters. OVAs store VM configurations and disks and can also be downloaded from the Nutanix environment.

tags.name: ImagePlacementPolicies
tags.description: It enables the creation and management of placement policies for image entities. Additionally, it allows the suspension and resumption of these policies. These policies ensure that images are placed on the targeted PEs according to the specified policies.

tags.name: ImageRateLimitPolicies
tags.description: It enables the creation and management of the rate limit policies for image entities. Additionally, it allows viewing the effective rate limit policy on all PEs. These policies ensure that bandwidth on the targeted PEs is used according to the policy when creating an image or while copying it from one PE to another.

tags.name: IscsiClients
tags.description: Represents the configuration of the external iSCSI client connecting to a Volume Group.  You can fetch and list iSCSI clients using these APIs.

tags.name: VolumeGroups
tags.description: Represents an entity that exposes block storage devices. Once created a Volume Group  may be either directly connected to a guest operating system or exposed to AHV hosts in a NCI  cluster. Storage & DR policies can be applied on a Volume Group by associating categories.

tags.name: NvmfClients
tags.description: NVMe-TCP, also known as NVMf or NVMe-oF, is an I/O protocol. NVMe over fabrics, where the fabrics can be TCP/IP, RDMA or fibre channel. The endpoints under this section represents the configuration of the external NVMe-TCP client connecting to a Volume Group. You can fetch and list NVMe-TCP clients using these APIs.
